newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on soybeans and weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on soybeans and weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a rally in soybean futures tied to concerns about dry weather in portions of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
New crop December touched a session high of $2.69-1/2 per bushel, near a three-month high and the highest level for that month since $2.73-1/2 was reached on May 12.
"It's the weather. We had the pause that refreshes yesterday and now we're right back into it, it's all off of the dry weather," said Dean Witter's Vic Lespinasse.

Meteorologists early Thursday said farmers in parts of the U.S. Midwest are expected to see high temperatures and no significant rain for the next seven days, further stressing a corn crop now in the pollination stage of development.

"There appears to be no significant rain for the dry areas of central and southern Illinois, parts of central and southwestern Indiana, eastern Missouri and eastern Iowa for the next seven to ten days," Weather Services Corp meteorologist Mike Palmerino said. "This weather will continue to raise concerns about this year's corn production in those states."
Corn ended 1-1/2 to 4-3/4 cents a bushel higher with September up 3-1/4 at $2.65-1/2. December was up 4-1/4 at $2.67-3/4.
Three U.S. corn yield contracts traded with the September down one bushel per acre at 131.5 and January was down 1.5 bushels per acre at 132.0.
Gains were limited by USDA's weekly export sales report Thursday that showed net export sales of old crop and new crop corn below expectations.

USDA said net export sales of old crop corn during the week ended July 24 totalled a minus 11,800 tonnes, below expectations for 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes. Sales of new crop corn totalled 147,700 tonnes, below expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
Funds bought at least 25.0 million bushels of corn with Merrill Lynch Futures the key purchaser of eight million bushels of December and six million bushels of March, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold three million bushels of December, Refco Inc sold six million bushels of December and bought three million bushels of December, traders said.

In spread dealings, Term Commodities did one million bushels of September/December at two cents, premium December, traders said. Rosenthal Collins did nearly one million bushels of September/December at two cents, premium December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above the 95,019 traded Wednesday.

In corn options, E.D. and F. Man International sold 2,000 December $2.50 calls at 22-1/2 cents, Cargill Investor Services sold 500 December $2.70 puts at 16-1/2 cents and LIT America sold 499 December $2.40 puts at four cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 34,000 contracts, below the 40,869 traded Wednesday.
